route_note: R1: Kokkos' own CMake build at the exact commits (af65233184 buggy, 71761882dc fixed; Kokkos 3.7.99), CUDA backend + Serial, CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release (-O3 -DNDEBUG), -lineinfo through CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS, nvcc_wrapper as CXX, embedded with add_subdirectory in a 4-line CMake project whose only target is the driver (Kokkos::kokkoscore); same flags and scripts for both variants. Deviations, all outside the kernel file (core/src/Cuda/Kokkos_Cuda_ReduceScan.hpp is untouched, no Kokkos source edited): (1) arch: this revision has no Kokkos_ARCH_ADA89 keyword (the record's option does not exist yet; only up to HOPPER90), so Kokkos_ARCH_AMPERE86=ON plus a wrapper around nvcc_wrapper that rewrites -arch=sm_86 to -arch=sm_89 (derived from $RW_NVCC_FLAGS); the driver has 18 cubins sm_89 plus compute_89 PTX, no sm_86. (2) CUDA 13.4 incompatibilities of the 2022 sources, worked around with a compat PRE-INCLUDE (rw_cuda_compat.h via NVCC_APPEND_FLAGS='-include ...', declarations only; identical for both variants): without it the build fails with core/src/Cuda/Kokkos_Cuda_Half_Conversion.hpp: 'no suitable user-defined conversion from "Kokkos::Experimental::half_t" to "__half" exists' / '__half2double is undefined' (8 errors per TU) and core/src/Cuda/Kokkos_CudaSpace.cpp(657): 'no suitable constructor exists to convert from "int" to "cudaMemLocation"' / 'argument of type "cudaStream_t" is incompatible with parameter of type "unsigned int"' (cudaMemPrefetchAsync signature changed in CUDA 13). (3) relocatability: the driver is relinked with the static CUDA runtime and RPATH=/opt/ohpc/pub/compiler/gcc/12.4.0/lib64 (Kokkos links the shared libcudart.so.13 without rpath); it needs only libcuda.so.1 + system libs. The tree is exported with simd/ and tpls/ (desul atomics) in addition to core/containers/algorithms. The -lineinfo SASS check of route R1 is owned by helper C: see targets/hecbench-dxtc2-1/lineinfo.check (RESULT SAME).
driver: driver.cpp: TestRepeatedTeamReduce from the fix commit's core/unit_test/TestTeam.hpp pasted verbatim (it does not exist at the parent) into a stand-alone main, with only: ncol (league size) 1500 -> 8, outer repetitions 100 -> 1, ASSERT_EQ replaced by a printed check. Per team: 10 iterations x 2 TeamThreadRange parallel_reduce (nlev = 129, cos/sin sums) + Kokkos::single; team size = team_size_recommended - 1 (non power of two); then a RangePolicy reduce that checks v(i) == v(0) + i. Kernel: cuda_parallel_launch_local_memory<ParallelFor<TestRepeatedTeamReduce<Cuda>, TeamPolicy<Cuda>, Cuda>> (T_KERNEL=TestRepeatedTeamReduce). Prints 'kokkos-6 driver: league=8 team_size=<n> (recommended <m>)' and a final line with the number of inconsistent columns (nonzero would be the symptom of the race, not a harness failure; the exit code is always 0).
input: league 8 teams, team size = recommended-1 (127 on the sm_75 smoke GPU; about 255 expected on sm_89, the exact value is printed by the run), 10 x 2 team reductions per team, 129 levels. Estimate: per reduction about 5 shared accesses per thread (store by <= 4 threads, 4 loads by every thread, a few join RMWs) x 20 reductions x <= 1023 threads x 8 teams <= 1e6 thread-level accesses (code-based estimate, not measured), below 1e7.
notes: Smoke on c38 (sm_75 rebuild via rw.sh smoke, NOT the deliverable): buggy and fixed both rc=0, 'kokkos-6 driver: league=8 team_size=127 (recommended 128)' and 'columns inconsistent: 0' (the race did not show on the sm_75 smoke run; it is nondeterministic and needs the sm_89 run plus the detector anyway). sm_89 artifacts: /mnt/beegfs/fzheng4/realworld/build/kokkos-6/{buggy,fixed}/driver (+ build_flags.txt, cmake_args.txt; the compile line shows -arch=sm_86, rewritten to sm_89 by the wrapper). The racing code is inlined twice into the team kernel (two reductions per iteration, sh_result shared between them because both are double sums); the SASS shows no barrier between the L118 reads of reduction 1 and the L105 store of reduction 2 in the buggy variant and a BAR.SYNC from L119 in the fixed one (see the oracle). As in the original test the team size is recommended-1 (non power of two); the missing barrier is unordered for any team size above 32 threads. No environment variables needed.
